subject: Private offer pricing: regional floor, pass-through for channel partners
messages:
From: Hannah Lee <h.lee@acme-cloud.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private offer question — regional floors + channel pass-through

Irene / Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed by the latency numbers. Procurement is preparing the internal PO and we need two clarifications to finish the paperwork:

1) Can the private offer support regional "floors" (we bill customers by region and need different list prices in EU vs US)? We want the contract to allow price parity exceptions by region rather than a single global list price.

2) How do you expect channel partner margin to be handled on private offers? Tom at CloudBroker asked whether we can emit an invoice that shows the reseller margin as a separate line, or if Redwood will net the reseller fee and send a single invoice to Acme. That affects our internal GL mapping.

I've attached our draft PO and a quick regional pricing spreadsheet — not final, just to show what our finance team expects. Can one of you confirm what options we have so we can rep them back to procurement?

Best,
Hannah
Hannah Lee
Head of Platform Partnerships
Acme Cloud

Attachments: Acme_PO_Draft_v1.pdf, regional-pricing-model.xlsx

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Lee <h.lee@acme-cloud.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer question — regional floors + channel pass-through

Hi Hannah — thanks for the clear ask and the attachments. Short answers up front, followed by recommended language and options.

1) Regional floors: Yes — we can issue private offers that define per-region list prices. We call these "regional price tiers" in our ops. The practical implications: the private-offer payload will include a region->SKU price mapping and the marketplace will enforce per-region pricing. Two caveats:
  - Not all marketplaces allow billing in a different currency without extra registration steps (esp. EU VAT).
  - If you want automatic fallback (e.g., use US price when EU capacity exhausted), we need to set an explicit fallback policy.

2) Channel pass-through: We support two patterns:
  - Gross invoice: Redwood invoices Acme for full list price and separately issues a partner payout to CloudBroker (requires an MPN-style payout workflow and adds reconciliation steps).
  - Net invoicing: Redwood invoices Acme net of reseller margin and pays CloudBroker separately; easier for Acme GL but less transparent for the partner.

Recommended: For speed, go with Gross invoice + partner payout. That preserves audit trails for procurement and lets CloudBroker receive a visible fee line. If Acme prefers a consolidated single invoice, we can do Net invoicing but would need PO language that indicates partner fee will be handled off-invoice or via credit note.

I've put a suggested PO clause at the end of this email you can drop into procurement. Ben / Laura — can you confirm marketplace constraints (currency/locale registration) and whether our billing team needs any PO-level triggers to flip between Gross vs Net?

--
Irene Choi
Director, Cloud GTM (Redwood Inference)
irene.choi@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

Suggested PO language:
"Redwood Inference will issue regional private-offer pricing mapped to Acme Cloud's specified regions. Redwood will provide itemized invoices showing list price and any partner payouts; partner margins will be disbursed to named channel partners under separate payout schedules, unless the parties agree in writing to consolidated net invoicing."

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Hannah Lee <h.lee@acme-cloud.com>, Tom Wu <tom.wu@cloudbroker.io>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 08:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer question — regional floors + channel pass-through

Looping in to confirm ops detail. Quick notes:

- Marketplace registration: Acme will need to ensure the buying entity is registered in each target marketplace locale for per-region billing. For AWS/GCP that's usually straightforward; for Azure there may be reseller registration requirements that take ~10 business days.
- Billing artifact options: If Acme wants an invoice with a visible partner fee line, we can produce it (gross invoice). That will require CloudBroker to be listed as the payout recipient in our partner system and we will need a signed W-9 or equivalent (depending on country) from CloudBroker.
- If Acme wants net invoicing, ops needs an explicit PO field: "Consolidated Billing: TRUE" so we know to net out the partner fee. Otherwise we default to Gross.

I've attached a one-page ops checklist (internal) with the steps and required docs — happy to share with Acme's procurement if useful.

-Ben

Attachments: marketplace-ops-checklist.pdf

From: Hannah Lee <h.lee@acme-cloud.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Tom Wu <tom.wu@cloudbroker.io>, procurement@acme-cloud.com
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 10:09:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer question — regional floors + channel pass-through

Thanks — this is great context. Procurement has two follow-ups:

1) Can you confirm whether the regional price tiers will require a separate private-offer per region, or a single bundle with a region mapping? They prefer a single contract if possible.

2) For the gross invoice flow, can Redwood include a separate line item for "Partner: CloudBroker" with the amount, so our AP can code it correctly? If so, what docs do you need from Tom to set that up?

We can sign the non-substantive commercial summary this week if we can get those answers.

Hannah

Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 16:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer question — regional floors + channel pass-through

Quick note from the partner side: we can provide the W-9 (US) and the partner form required by Redwood. Our preference is gross invoicing with a visible partner line — makes downstream revenue share reporting simpler on our end. If Acme's AP needs the partner line to be a separate invoiceable line, we can accept either a Redwood-disbursed payout or a short partner invoice (we're flexible).

Action items we need from Redwood to close this week:
- Confirmation that a single contract + regional price mapping is supported (preferred).
- The exact PO field name/value to trigger net vs gross invoicing (Ben mentioned "Consolidated Billing: TRUE").
- A list of docs Redwood needs to wire the partner payout (W-9, bank details, partner ID).

Tom Wu
Head of Partnerships
CloudBroker
+1 (206) 555-0147
